q: How is this different from Strimzi?
a: Strimzi is an excellent operator for a single Kubernetes cluster. [BRAND] runs a single Kafka quorum across 3+ Kubernetes clusters via the Kubernetes Multi-Cluster Services (MCS) API — works on Submariner, Cilium Cluster Mesh, Istio multi-cluster, or any other compliant implementation. And it ships the platform pieces (Kroxylicious proxy with OIDC RBAC, Apicurio with a JWT-aware RBAC proxy, MirrorMaker2 with schema-id rewriting, Cruise Control, declarative backup/restore, and a UI) as first-class CRDs. With Strimzi you assemble those from 5–6 separate Helm charts.

q: Does it require KRaft? Can I still run ZooKeeper?
a: KRaft only, Apache Kafka 4.x and later. ZooKeeper is removed from Kafka 4.0 — there's no ZooKeeper path to support.

q: What does the multi-cluster setup require?
a: Three or more Kubernetes clusters joined via any MCS-compatible mesh — Submariner Lighthouse, Cilium Cluster Mesh, and Istio multi-cluster all work. Brokers stay local to a cluster; controllers form one quorum across clusters via *.svc.clusterset.local — the standard MCS DNS namespace.

q: Can I run it on a single cluster?
a: Yes. Multi-cluster is opt-in. A single-cluster deployment is just one entry in spec.clusters[] and needs no MCS mesh at all.
Apache 2.0, end to end. Operator, Kroxylicious filters, Apicurio RBAC proxy, MM2 schema transfer SMT, backup wrapper, Kafka UI — all in the same repo, all Apache 2.0.
Kubernetes 1.28+. Tested on Kind, GKE, EKS, and AKS.

q: How does the proxy RBAC work?
a: Clients hit Kroxylicious instead of brokers directly. A custom filter extracts the JWT, maps realm_access.roles to groups, and authorizes topic/group operations using ACLs you declare in a KafkaRbac CR. The same JWT also authorizes schema-registry artifact access via the Apicurio RBAC proxy.

q: How do you handle rolling restarts safely?
a: Every restart goes through an ISR + KRaft quorum check. The operator refuses to restart a broker while partitions are under-replicated or the controller quorum would lose majority. Cross-cluster roll ordering is declared explicitly via spec.clusterRollOrder.

A KafkaBackup CR builds a CronJob that streams topic records and consumer offsets (optionally Apicurio schemas) to S3, Azure Blob, GCS, or a PVC. KafkaRestore is an idempotent one-shot Job with point-in-time recovery and topic remapping.

q: Is the included UI just for read access?
a: No. The KafkaUI CR deploys kafka-editor — a React 19 + Quarkus 3.17 console with topic CRUD, message produce, consumer-group reset, and schema browsing. Every action is gated by the same KafkaRbac as your real Kafka clients: OIDC login at the browser, JWT propagated to the proxy via SASL/OAUTHBEARER on every backend call. No admin backdoor, and every write is audited per user.

Every authorization decision in the Kroxylicious proxy and the Apicurio RBAC proxy, plus every write in kafka-editor. One JSON record shape across all three emitters (principal, groups, operation, resource, decision, latency, correlation id) on the SLF4J channel kafka-audit (and kafka-editor.audit for the editor). Stdout is always on; an opt-in __audit Kafka topic ships records into Loki, OpenSearch, Splunk, or BigQuery via Kafka Connect. There is no separate audit gateway to bypass.
